content.rationale:
This decision models the commit policy of a discard as Quint state: one call over the draft registry, in `specs/drafts/discard_commit.qnt` (module `draft_discard_commit`), in the house form of `specs/drafts/discard.qnt` and `specs/drafts/state.qnt` - a module that imports the state model and the registry action it stands in front of, and steps the registry variable `records`, with the one action as its only export. The check `specs/drafts/discard_commit_check.qnt` (mnoutqtq) fixes the interface this module must carry - `action discardCommit(handles: List[str], prepared: Set[str], failed: bool)` over `records`, total over its three inputs - and the module supplies exactly that action. The check reads no helper from the module, and the module defines none of the check's own `gate`-prefixed helpers (`gateNamed`, `gateAccepted`, `gateWithoutNamed`, `gateCommitReady`), whose names the flattened TLA+ module would otherwise share.

nwswzlnw fixes where the commit sits, and the module states exactly that. The registry removal is the commit point and it is taken last, only after every named draft's change act, workspace act and directory act have completed. So a call reaches the commit only when nothing failed before it and every named draft is prepared: `prepared` is the set of named handles whose three acts have completed before the call decides, and `failed` says whether any of those acts, or the removal itself while no record had yet left the store, failed before the commit. `commitReached` is therefore `not(failed)`, every named handle contained in `prepared`, and every named handle an `open` record. Before that point the call steps `records` to itself, so a failure at any act or at the removal leaves the registry exactly as it stood: every named draft's record is still at its handle and still `open`, and every other record is untouched. The refusal does not reach back to unmake an act that already completed, because the module fixes what the store holds after a failure, not an order of undo.

qmpskomv fixes the selection and the removal, and the module imports them literally rather than restating them: `discardNamed` reads the handle list as a set, so a handle named twice is one handle and the order of the list carries no meaning; `discardAccepted` holds exactly when every named handle picks out an `open` record; and `discardWithout` is the registry with exactly the named handles removed. The commit is that accepted removal and no other: a landed record or a handle the registry does not hold reaches no commit, an empty call is accepted and removes nothing, and prepared handles the call does not name do not widen the removal. There is no third outcome and no per-handle partial removal - a call either leaves the registry exactly as it was or steps it to exactly qmpskomv's registry without every named handle - and because the whole effect is one assignment of one variable, the removal is one act of the invocation rather than a sequence of removals.

tvtnokzu fixes the record's shape, its two states `open` and `landed`, and the registry map `records`; the module imports all of that from `draft_state` and restates none of it - no field, no state value, no constructor, no base and no transition of the record is defined here, and the action steps no variable but `records`. Outside the module, because each is another decision and none is needed to state this one: the order of the change, workspace and directory acts among themselves; what the change act does when it gives up a change; the workspace forget, the directory removal and the paths they touch, which nwswzlnw leaves to the workspace half and the change act; the jj invocations; the verb surface, its wording, streams and exit status; the registry write's own mechanism, partial-write, atomicity and durability, which begins only after a record has left the store; and how a real discard abandons the change and forgets the workspace, which this model does not perform.

The module is carried as Quint because the house checks decisions of this kind by running them: the record and its lifecycle are already a machine artifact (tvtnokzu) and the registry action is one too (qmpskomv), so the commit policy can be read as one guard in front of that action and model-checked. The check's seeded registry, call pool, invariants and runs are the check's; this node states the behaviour, and no verdict about a run is content of it.
